name: Hyperprolinemia Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biochemical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Hyperprolinemia Type 1

criteria.description: Persistent elevated plasma proline concentration above normal reference range
Demonstration of reduced proline dehydrogenase enzyme activity in fibroblasts or leukocytes
Identification of pathogenic variants in the PRODH gene by molecular genetic testing
Presence of neurological symptoms such as seizures or developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated plasma proline plus either reduced proline dehydrogenase activity or pathogenic PRODH gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by biochemical testing combined with genetic analysis.

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated serum ammonia
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes
other: Reduced proline dehydrogenase enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts or leukocytes

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic facial features and cardiac anomalies

redFlags: Early onset seizures refractory to treatment
Severe cognitive impairment with metabolic abnormalities
references: Hodgkinson et al., Hyperprolinemia Type 1: Clinical and Molecular Aspects, J Inherit Metab Dis, 2020
Orphanet Report Series: Hyperprolinemia Type 1, Orphanet, 2023
